 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before

On The 5 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 17069 of 2023
 Smt. Siya Devi And Others
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Asha Ram Shivhare - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri A.P.S. Tomar - Pp for the respondent/State.
 Shri H.K. Shukla - Advocate for respondent No.2.
 Order

The present petition under section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR registered at Police Station Dabra District Gwalior vide Crime No.600/2022 under section 498-A, 506, 34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and added 377 of IPC and consequential proceedings arising out of the same.

2. Short facts of the case are that the complainant (Respondent No. 2) was married to Petitioner No.
3, the son of Petitioners No. 1 and 2, on 07.05.2015, according to Hindu rites and rituals.
Following the marriage, it is alleged that her husband and his family members began to harass her in connection with a demand for Rs.5,00,000/- as dowry.
During the subsistence of the marriage, the complainant gave birth to a female child, who is presently five years old.

Despite this, the alleged harassment NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31783 2 MCRC-17069-2023 continued,
and ultimately, on 03.06.2022, the complainant was allegedly forced out of her matrimonial home.
Subsequently, on 13.07.2022, she lodged an FIR against all the petitioners.
After investigation, the police filed a charge-sheet against them.
The matter is currently pending before the trial Court.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that they are innocent and have been falsely implicated.

The criminal proceedings are frivolous and deserve to be quashed, especially as the Smt. Siya Devi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30895131/

sentences.text: complainant
has initiated them as a counterblast to earlier proceedings filed by her husband.
Due to the complainant's non-cooperative behaviour, the petitioners had approached police authorities multiple times between 2016-2022.

Though the complainant claims she was ousted on 03.06.2022,
the FIR was lodged only on 13.07.2022, without any reasonable explanation.
Petitioners No. 1 and 2 (parents of petitioner No. 3) live separately at Sheopur, while petitioner No. 3 lives in Gwalior; yet they were implicated only because of their relationship.

4. It is further submitted that the complainant previously lodged an FIR under Sections 498A, 323,
506, 342, 34 IPC in 2015, in which the petitioners were acquitted on 04.01.2016.
This crucial fact was suppressed in the present FIR.

The FIR contains general, non-specific allegations without dates,
details, or particular acts attributable to the petitioners.
The FIR appears pre- planned and malicious, filed only to victimise the petitioners, warranting quashing at the threshold.

Despite filing the present FIR, the complainant filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act on 22.08.2022, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31783 3 MCRC-17069-2023 seeking restitution of conjugal rights, which contradicts her allegations.
The FIR contained no allegation under Section 377 IPC, but the complainant later developed a new story, leading to its addition in the charge-sheet, showing afterthought and malice.
The complainant had already withdrawn her cases under Section 125 Cr.P.C. and the Domestic Violence Act, indicating resolution of earlier disputes.

In support of his submissions, learned counsel placed reliance in the matter of Rafiq Khan and anr. Vs. Jamila Bee and anr. reported in 1999(1)MPLJ 724 and in the matter of Ashish Vs. State of M.P. and another reported in 2015(1)MPWN 188 .
5.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the complainant submitted that from bare perusal of the contents of the FIR prima facie the offence under the section mentioned therein are made out against the present petitioners, and therefore, the prayer made by the counsel for the petitioners for quashing the FIR should not be acceded to.
Thus, it was prayed that present petition be dismissed.

6. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

This Court, relying on the decision in Manish Sahu vs. State of Madhya Pradesh (MCRC No.
8388/2023, decided on 01.05.2024) , reiterates that allegations of marital rape or unnatural sexual acts between a husband and wife residing together during the subsistence of a valid marriage do not attract Section 377 IPC.

With respect to Section 498-A IPC, it is noted that the petitioners were earlier tried and acquitted for the same offence on identical facts by judgment dated 04.01.2016, which has attained finality.

In such circumstances, prosecution on the same set of allegations is barred under Section 300(1)
Cr.P.C.
Furthermore, the present FIR contains only vague, omnibus, and general allegations, with suppression of material facts.
